script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

Title: CHANGE OF PACE

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

A quiet coffee shop filled with the aroma of freshly ground beans.

SAM, mid-30s, a frazzled marketing executive, sits alone at a table, hunched over his laptop. He looks up at the clock, frustrated. Five hours and still no progress on his latest campaign.

Suddenly, the door swings open and in walks a woman - RACHEL, late 20s, wearing a bohemian dress and a wide-brimmed hat. Her eyes light up as she takes in the scene. She approaches the counter and orders an herbal tea.

As she waits, she notices Sam's tense expression.

RACHEL
(cheerfully)
You look like you could use a break. What's got you so worked up?

SAM
(sighs)
Just another marketing campaign that's going nowhere. I'm starting to feel like I'm in a rut.

Rachel sets down her tea and sits across from Sam.

RACHEL
I know exactly how you feel. I used to be just like you, climbing the corporate ladder, but it wasn't fulfilling me. One day, I just decided to take a chance and follow my passion.

Sam raises an eyebrow.

SAM
And what's that?

RACHEL
I've always loved art, so I started selling my paintings online. It's not easy, but every sale is worth it.

Sam leans back, intrigued.

SAM
That sounds nice, but I don't have a passion like that. I don't even know where to start.

Rachel smiles sympathetically.

RACHEL
Well, maybe I can help you figure it out. I've got some free time this week if you want to explore some new hobbies together.

INT. ART SUPPLY STORE - DAY

The smell of paint and canvas fills the air as Sam and Rachel browse the shelves.

RACHEL
(pointing to a set of watercolors)
How about trying your hand at watercolors? They're very forgiving.

SAM
(laughs)
I don't even know the first thing about painting.

RACHEL
That's where I come in. I'll teach you everything I know.

INT. PARK - DAY

The sun filters through the trees as Sam and Rachel sit on a blanket, painting the scenery around them.

SAM
(struggling with his brush)
I don't think I have a creative bone in my body.

RACHEL
(smiling)
Everyone has creativity within them. It just takes practice to bring it out.

Sam looks at his painting, surprised by the colors and shapes emerging on the page.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

Sam and Rachel sit at the same table, their laptops open in front of them.

SAM
I've been thinking... maybe I could start selling my paintings online, like you suggested.

RACHEL
(grins)
That's the spirit! I believe in you.

INT. SAM'S APARTMENT - DAY

Sam sits at his kitchen table, surrounded by stacks of paintings. He's determined to make this work.

SAM
(to himself)
I can do this.

INT. ART GALLERY - NIGHT

Sam stands in front of a crowd, nervously clutching a microphone. He's just given a speech about his artwork and is now open for questions.

SAM
(smiling)
Any questions?

A young woman raises her hand.

WOMAN
How did you find the courage to leave your old career and pursue art?

Sam looks around the room, then back at the woman.

SAM
I had help from someone who believed in me when I didn't believe in myself. And I learned that it's never too late to make a change.

The crowd applauds, and Sam takes a deep breath, feeling a sense of pride and accomplishment.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
